2607.27177.title: Partner Capability Estimation for Task-Agnostic Adaptation in Ad-Hoc Teamwork
2607.27177.paper_summary: Effective collaboration with novel and diverse partners is a crucial skill for autonomous agents. Most current ad-hoc teamwork (AHT) approaches assume that agents will collaborate on a single, fixed task and that the partner's capabilities, their ability to successfully execute the desired action, are already known. In reality, a partner's true capabilities are often hidden, and human collaborators may act sub-optimally on tasks with multiple valid strategies. To address these limitations, we extend ad-hoc teamwork into a multi-task setting by re-framing it as a problem of joint planning with decentralised execution under hidden partner capabilities. We introduce CE-CM (Capability Estimation via Contextual Models), an approximate Bayesian method that infers task-invariant capability vectors. By using simulation-based sampling, the agent estimates capabilities and induces a contextual Multi-agent Markov Decision Processes for planning. This approach requires no population pre-training and refines its beliefs online from just a few tasks. To account for human unpredictability, we propose CE-CM-Div, an extension that evaluates capability hypotheses against diverse planner rollouts rather than a single optimal trajectory. Simulated experiments demonstrate that CE-CM rapidly recovers hidden capabilities, reduces infeasible action assignments, and adapts to changes over time. Furthermore, in an offline human study of 225 trajectories from 15 participants, CE-CM-Div substantially improved capability estimates over the baseline CE-CM method. Our results suggest capability-based modelling is a promising interpretable, task-agnostic representation in the studied settings, demonstrating that accounting for behavioural diversity is essential for robust human-AI teaming.
2607.27177.paper_summary_zh: 有效與新穎且多樣的夥伴合作是自主代理的重要技能。大多數當前的臨時團隊合作（AHT）方法假設代理將在單一固定任務上合作，並且夥伴的能力、他們成功執行所需行動的能力，已經是已知的。實際上，夥伴的真實能力往往是隱藏的，而人類合作夥伴在多種有效策略的任務上可能會表現不佳。為了解決這些限制，我們將臨時團隊合作擴展到多任務環境，將其重新框定為在隱藏夥伴能力下的聯合規劃與去中心化執行的問題。我們引入了CE-CM（透過情境模型的能力估計），這是一種近似的貝葉斯方法，用於推斷任務不變的能力向量。通過使用基於模擬的抽樣，代理估計能力並引導出一個情境多代理馬爾可夫決策過程以進行規劃。這種方法不需要人口預訓練，並且能夠從僅幾個任務中在線精煉其信念。為了考慮人類的不可預測性，我們提出了CE-CM-Div，這是一種擴展，通過評估能力假設對多樣化的規劃者滾動而不是單一最佳軌跡。模擬實驗顯示，CE-CM能迅速恢復隱藏的能力，減少不可行的行動分配，並隨著時間的推移適應變化。此外，在一項對15名參與者的225條軌跡進行的離線人類研究中，CE-CM-Div顯著改善了相較於基線CE-CM方法的能力估計。我們的結果表明，基於能力的建模在所研究的環境中是一種有前景的可解釋的、任務無關的表示，顯示考慮行為多樣性對於穩健的人機團隊合作至關重要。
